guideCenter.faq1Title: The device keeps failing to connect/is frequently disconnected?
guideCenter.faq1Point1: ① Server address and port: Based on the MQTT address in the platform configuration or device details, select the port according to the connection method (MQTT plain text 1883 / MQTTS encryption 8883 / WebSocket 8083 / 8084), and confirm that the network where the device is located has released the corresponding port.
guideCenter.faq1Point2: ② ClientID format: must be "product ID&device name" (& connector in the middle), both product ID and device name can be copied on the platform.
guideCenter.faq1Point3: ③ Username expiry: The fourth segment is a Unix timestamp in seconds. An expired username is rejected; choose a suitable validity period.
guideCenter.faq1Point4: ④ Password signature: Base64-decode the device secret into the raw key, sign the username with HMAC-SHA1, then append ";hmacsha1". Authentication fails if these steps are done in the wrong order.
guideCenter.faq1Point5: ⑤ Device status: Confirm that the device is not disabled and the product is not deactivated.
guideCenter.faq1Point6: ⑥ Quick check: Connect with MQTTX or another MQTT client using the same credentials. This separates credential problems from device code problems. Then check the device status and logs.
guideCenter.faq2Title: The device is online but cannot see the data?
guideCenter.faq2Point1: ① Field name verification: The field name reported in JSON must be exactly the same as the "identifier" of the object model function (case sensitive). If the identifier is temperature, Temperature cannot be reported.
guideCenter.faq2Point2: ② Report Topic: Publish properties to $thing/up/property/{'{productID}'}/{'{deviceName}'}. The platform will not parse messages sent to another Topic.
guideCenter.faq2Point3: ③ Custom protocol: Confirm that the protocol script has been bound to the product and the decoding logic is correct; the conversion results can be debugged online using simulated messages in the protocol script details.
guideCenter.faq2Point4: ④ View original messages: Enter the device details "Log" page, view the original upstream/downstream messages of the device, and confirm whether the data reaches the platform and what the analysis result is.
guideCenter.faq3Title: Does the reported data value not match the actual value?
guideCenter.faq3Point1: ① Field mix-up: Compare every reported field with its thing model identifier. Do not send one property value under another identifier.
guideCenter.faq3Point2: ② Magnification and unit: The object model defines the unit (such as ℃, kWh), and the device reports the original value; if conversion is required (such as 0.1℃ accuracy), it is completed first when decoding the protocol script.
guideCenter.faq3Point3: ③ Enumeration and Boolean: The value of the enumeration type must correspond one-to-one with the enumeration item defined by the object model; use true/false for Boolean.
guideCenter.faq3Point4: ④ Comparison and troubleshooting: Check the latest value and the original log message at the same time on the "Object Model" page of the device details to confirm whether it is a reported problem or an analysis problem.
guideCenter.faq4Title: How can I provision devices in bulk?
guideCenter.faq4Point1: ① Turn on "Dynamic Registration" in the product details to obtain the product key (ProductSecret).
guideCenter.faq4Point2: ② When the device is powered on for the first time, use the product key to exchange for the key of the device through the HTTP/MQTT dynamic registration interface (see the "Device Access" page of the product details for interface and signature examples).
guideCenter.faq4Point3: ③ After getting the device key, connect to the platform according to the standard process; all devices under the same product can burn the same product key, and there is no need to enter it one by one.
guideCenter.faq4Point4: ④ Security suggestions: The product key is only used for first-time registration. The registration interface has signature and timestamp verification to prevent forgery.
guideCenter.faq5Title: How to access the gateway and sub-devices?
guideCenter.faq5Point1: ① Create two products respectively: gateway product (select "Gateway" as the device type) and sub-device product (select "Sub-device" as the device type).
guideCenter.faq5Point2: ② The sub-device cannot be directly connected to the platform and needs to rely on gateway communication (supports Zigbee/BLE/433/custom and other gateway protocols, select on the product).
guideCenter.faq5Point3: ③ After the gateway device is online and the sub-device topology is added, the platform will maintain the hierarchical relationship between the gateway and the sub-device; the sub-device data is transparently transmitted to the cloud through the gateway.
guideCenter.faq5Point4: ④ The connection parameters of the gateway itself can be viewed in the gateway device details; the object model definition of the sub-device is completely consistent with the directly connected device.
guideCenter.faq6Title: The alarm was triggered but no one received the notification?
guideCenter.faq6Point1: ① Confirm that the alarm rule has been "enabled" and the trigger conditions match the device data (you can first manually adjust the threshold to the range that must be triggered to verify the link).
guideCenter.faq6Point2: ② Notification link: Rule hit → Generate alarm event → Assemble message according to "Notification content template" → Send to contact through notification channel; Check whether the configuration is complete step by step.
guideCenter.faq6Point3: ③ Notification channels and contacts are configured by the administrator in the system management "Notification Management" (SMS/Email/Webhook, etc.).
guideCenter.faq6Point4: ④ Locate the cause of failure: Enter "Alarm Management → Notification Record" to view the sending status and failure reason of each notification.

pageGuide.productListSummary: A product groups devices of the same type. Define its thing model once so its devices can connect using the same template.
pageGuide.productListPoints1: Standard device onboarding: create a product → define its thing model → create a device → connect it → view data.
pageGuide.productListPoints2: The product details page generates its access parameters, including product ID, secret, server address and code examples, for use on the device.

pageGuide.productListSections2Title: Three parts of a thing model
pageGuide.productListSections2Points1: Property: a persistent device state that can be read or set, such as power, target temperature or brightness.
pageGuide.productListSections2Points2: Event: information reported by a device that cannot be queried, classified as alarm, fault or information; it can include output parameters.
pageGuide.productListSections2Points3: Action: a remote operation invoked by the platform, with input and output parameters, such as unlocking while recording the operator and time.
pageGuide.productListSections3Points1: A product with devices cannot be deleted, preventing accidental loss of active devices.
pageGuide.productListSections3Points2: Properties and events of published products cannot be edited or deleted. Standard, inherited and custom functions have different editing permissions.
pageGuide.schemaSummary: A thing model (TSL) describes device capabilities at the product level using properties, events and actions. The platform uses it to parse and validate device data.
pageGuide.schemaPoints1: A function identifier is the unique key used in device data. A reported JSON field name must match it exactly, including case.
pageGuide.schemaPoints2: Product categories provide standard thing models for common devices. Select a category when creating a product to reuse its model.
pageGuide.schemaSections1Title: Definitions of the three function types
pageGuide.schemaSections1TableRows13: A state that persists when the device is running, and applications can initiate reading and writing
pageGuide.schemaSections1TableRows23: Information reported by a device that cannot be obtained by querying. Alarm, fault and information events can have multiple output parameters; applications cannot set events.
pageGuide.schemaSections1TableRows33: Remote actions invoked by the platform. They support input and output parameters and can be synchronous or asynchronous.
pageGuide.schemaSections1TableRows34: Restart, reset, and "romantic mode" to set color + brightness + color temperature at once

pageGuide.schemaSections2TableRows43: 0 turn off the light / 1 turn on the light

pageGuide.schemaSections2TableRows82: Nested arrays are not supported. Set the maximum length; access an element as propertyID.index, such as switch.1.
pageGuide.schemaSections3Points1: "Add standard function" is selected from the category/platform function library; "New custom function" is freely defined.
pageGuide.schemaSections3Points2: Standard functions cannot be edited; inherited product functions cannot be edited or deleted; custom functions can be edited or deleted.
pageGuide.schemaSections3Points3: Properties and events of published products cannot be edited and deleted, and the product release status needs to be processed first.
pageGuide.categorySummary: Categories hold standard thing models for common device types, such as temperature sensors and electricity meters.
pageGuide.categoryPoints1: Select a category when creating a product to inherit its standard thing model instead of defining every function individually.
pageGuide.categoryPoints2: Custom categories can hold standard models for your business domain, reusable by similar products.
pageGuide.categorySections1Points1: A category’s thing model is applied to products in that category and its subcategories. Inherited product functions cannot be edited or deleted on an individual product.
pageGuide.categorySections1Points2: Changing a category’s thing model affects products using it. Review this platform-wide change carefully.
pageGuide.categorySections1Points3: Plan the category hierarchy first, then define the standard functions at each level.
pageGuide.deviceListSummary: A device is an instance of a product. After creating it, use its device secret to connect and report data. Device Access in the details page provides copyable connection parameters.
pageGuide.deviceListPoints1: One device, one secret (recommended): create each device on the platform with its own secret for easier debugging and stronger isolation.
pageGuide.deviceListPoints2: One product, one secret (bulk provisioning): enable dynamic registration on the product. On first startup, the device exchanges the product secret for its own device secret.
pageGuide.deviceListPoints3: A new device moves from Inactive to Online or Offline. Its activation and last online times appear in the details page.
pageGuide.deviceListSections1Title: Verify access with MQTT X in five minutes
pageGuide.deviceListSections1Points1: ① Download the open source MQTT client MQTT X and create a new connection.
pageGuide.deviceListSections1Points2: ② Use the credentials from device details. ClientID is productID&deviceName (for example TXXXXDS8G&dev001). Username includes ClientID, version, random string and expiry timestamp; Password is generated by the signature rule. Copy the current values from Device Access.
pageGuide.deviceListSections1Points3: ③ Use the MQTT server address and port shown in Device Access for this device. Choose a plain or encrypted connection according to its configuration.
pageGuide.deviceListSections1Points4: ④ Subscribe to the downlink Topic and publish a property report. Verify the server response and compare the reported value with the platform thing model.
pageGuide.deviceListSections2Title: What you can do in device details
pageGuide.deviceListSections2Points1: Device Access: view and copy the device credentials and connection parameters. Provision the device secret on the device for secret authentication.
pageGuide.deviceListSections2Points2: Thing Model: view current and historical property values, update times, event records and action calls.
pageGuide.deviceListSections2Points3: Logs: inspect uplink and downlink messages and control commands when troubleshooting data.
pageGuide.deviceListSections2Points4: Online Debugging: the control panel is generated from the product thing model. Commands and device responses appear side by side.

pageGuide.protocolGatewaySummary: A protocol gateway connects devices that use third-party protocols. It translates device traffic for the platform message bus and translates platform commands back to the device protocol.
pageGuide.protocolGatewayPoints1: Uplink: device → protocol gateway → message bus → platform. Downlink: platform → message bus → gateway → device.
pageGuide.protocolGatewayPoints2: The gateway runs as a separate service. It registers with the platform and sends heartbeats; its status becomes Stopped after the heartbeat times out.
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections1Points1: ① Install the protocol gateway service in the deployment directory: docker compose -f docker-compose-protocol.yml up -d (or run from source with go run .).
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections1Points2: ② Check the gateway status in Data Flow → Protocol Gateway (Running or Stopped).
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections1Points3: ③ Some protocols need product-level settings, such as cloud account credentials. Configure them under Device Access in the product details.
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections1Points4: ④ Create a device for the protocol, then use its connection settings to test reporting with a compatible client.
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections2TableRows12: Alibaba Cloud alink, Tencent Cloud IoT, Zhongmin Cloud, telecom IoT platforms, China Mobile OneNet, Tuya Cloud (planned)
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections2TableRows22: Alibaba Cloud alink MQTT, Tencent Cloud MQTT, Modbus (TCP/UDP/RTU with point mapping), IEC 104 power protocol, Wumei MQTT (open source), Glansbay Bluetooth gateway, Zhonghong HVAC, VRF central air conditioning, EV chargers, Smart parking locks, Xiaozhi AI voice, Geological hazard monitoring
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections2TableRows32: GB28181 (SIP registration/preview/PTZ/playback), ONVIF (discovery/preview/PTZ/playback), RTSP-RTMP pull streaming
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections3Points1: Protocol gateway: a separately deployed conversion service for established protocols such as Modbus, GB28181 and cloud integrations, maintained by platform administrators.
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections3Points2: Protocol script: a lightweight Go script written in the platform for a product’s parsing, conversion or linkage logic.
pageGuide.protocolGatewaySections3Points3: Use an existing gateway when the protocol is supported; start with a script to validate a private protocol.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSummary: Alarm rules detect device anomalies. When data meets a trigger condition, the platform creates an alarm event, sends notifications and tracks resolution.
pageGuide.alarmRulePoints1: Configure a rule and severity → device data meets the condition → alarm event is created → a notification template sends messages → track resolution in the event.
pageGuide.alarmRulePoints2: Start with essential rules such as offline status or high temperature. Verify the event and notification flow before adding more.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections1Points1: Alarm rules: add or edit a rule in three steps (basic information, trigger conditions, confirmation), then enable or disable it.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections1Points2: Trigger condition templates: reuse conditions across rules; editing a shared template updates every rule that uses it.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections1Points3: Notification templates: define the message title, body and variables.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections1Points4: Alarm events: view events created when rules trigger and track their handling.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections1Points5: Notification records: check each delivery status here when a recipient did not receive an alert.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections1Points6: Resolution tracking: record actions and conclusions in the event details.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections2Points1: Name rules for the device and scenario, such as “Building 1 – High Temperature”, so events are easy to identify.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections2Points2: Create a reusable template for complex conditions instead of repeating the setup in each rule.
pageGuide.alarmRuleSections2Points3: Trigger each new rule with a real device or simulated data. Confirm the alarm event and notification delivery before production use.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSummary: Go scripts interpreted by yaegi process device uplink and downlink messages. They can convert, calculate and trigger device actions so the platform can handle messages that do not already match its thing model.
pageGuide.ruleScriptPoints1: Typical uses: parse generic MQTT messages, calculate values such as power from voltage × current or energy differences, handle special devices and control other devices from a script.
pageGuide.ruleScriptPoints2: Workflow: create a script and choose its type and source → edit it → debug it on the Script tab → bind a product or device on the Device tab and enable it → process messages.
pageGuide.ruleScriptPoints3: The script type selects a default template. Its func Handle function is the entry point; adapt the logic there.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections1Points1: Script type combines direction and timing. Uplink: device → preprocessing → platform parsing → postprocessing → platform data. Downlink: platform → preprocessing → device execution → postprocessing.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections1Points2: Choose a script type when creating the script. The platform inserts its template; the three templates use different Handle signatures (see below). A mismatched signature raises “struct must define: func Handle(...)”.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections1TableRows14: Rewrite the raw device report: parse, convert or filter it.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections1TableRows24: Use the messages before and after parsing for statistics, notifications or other side effects.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections1TableRows34: Rewrite the command sent from the platform to the device.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections1TableRows44: Record the delivery result or perform other follow-up work.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections2Points1: Operation source and operation type select the message bus channel where the script runs. They correspond to the handle/type fields of PublishMsg.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections2TableRows12: property: properties / event: events / action: actions / service: application services
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections2TableRows22: operation: get log level / report: report logs / update: push a log level change
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections2TableRows32: upgrade: send an upgrade message / progress: report device upgrade progress
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections2TableRows42: topo: manage topology / status: report child device online or offline status / thing: thing model operations
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections2TableRows52: ntp: network time / register: device registration
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections3Points1: The Handle parameter req contains the device message. Payload is its body, usually JSON for thing model messages. Rewrite Payload and return req to change the message.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections4Points1: Use import to access Go standard packages such as json, time and http directly. These platform packages cover common tasks:
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections4TableRows13: Print logs that appear in the page debugger.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections4TableRows33: Query devices, products and thing models.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections4TableRows43: Services for device control, device management, product management and OTA management.

pageGuide.ruleScriptSections4TableRows63: Full and simplified thing model definitions.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections5Title: Example 1: Parse a thing model property report
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections5Points1: A thing model property report has a JSON Payload with method=report. Parse it with deviceMsg.ThingReq, then read values by identifier for calculations.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections6Title: Example 2: Rewrite message fields with gjson
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections6Points1: Use gjson GetBytes/SetBytes/DeleteBytes to edit Payload fields. This example copies hc_on to hc_off, then removes hc_on.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections7Title: Example 3: Control another device with dm
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections7Points1: The dm package exposes platform functions to scripts. Query devices, products or thing models, or send a control command to another device.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections8Points1: ① Debug: on the detail page’s Script tab, choose string or hex content, a product and a device. Enter a raw message and select Debug. Check the transformed Payload in Results and log.Print output in Debug Logs.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections8Points2: ② Save the script after debugging succeeds.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections8Points3: ③ Bind: on the Device tab, add a binding and choose a product. Leave the device blank to cover every device in that product. Set a priority (smaller numbers run first) and enable the binding.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections8Points4: ④ Activation requires both an enabled script and an enabled binding. A script with Universal scope applies to all organizations.
pageGuide.ruleScriptSections8Points5: ⑤ Multiple scripts at the same execution point run in ascending priority order. Each script receives the previous script’s output.
